I've been growing cotton on these 7 mu for 45 years now. Last year I got about 260 jin per mu, which was decent but a bit low because of the dry spell in July. This year I'll stick with the same improved seed I bought last year — the Bt cotton from the seed dealer in town. It costs more than saving my own seed, but I saw what happened to Old Wang's field when he tried to save seed from the hybrid — the bollworm ate half his crop. Not worth the risk.

For fertilizer, I learned from the village extension training a few years back that they recommend about 15 kg of pure nitrogen per mu. But I always put down a bit more because last year when I cut back to save money, the plants looked yellow and the yield dropped. I'll apply 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that's half a bag, gives me about 8 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium. Then I'll topdress twice with urea, about 15 kg each time, which adds another 7 kg or so of nitrogen. So in total I'm looking at about 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I know it's a little more than the book says, but I'd rather waste some fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad year means I can't pay for my wife's medicine.

For irrigation, I have my own well, but pumping costs electricity. Last year I irrigated three times — once before planting to get the soil moist, once at flowering in July, and once when the bolls were filling in August. This year I'll do the same unless it rains heavily. Three times is what my neighbor Li does on his 8 mu, and his cotton always looks better than mine.

Pesticide is the big cost for cotton. I spray five times: once before planting for soil pests, twice for bollworm in July, once for aphids, and once for mites in August. I use the same chemicals the dealer recommends — I don't know all the names, but I know the red bottle and the blue bottle. Each spray costs me about 25 yuan per mu, so that's 125 yuan per mu just for pesticide. But without it, the bollworm will destroy everything.

For tillage, I hire the rotary tiller from the village machinery cooperative. It costs 40 yuan per mu and saves my back. I till once in mid-April before planting.

My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends some money home, so I have a little cash. But I still need to be careful — fertilizer prices went up again this year. If I spend too much on inputs, I won't have money for hiring pickers in the fall. Cotton picking is all hired labor now since it's just me and my wife. Last year I paid 1.2 yuan per jin for picking, and that cost me over 600 yuan per mu. So every yuan I spend on fertilizer or pesticide is a yuan I don't have for picking.

I expect about 280 kg per mu this year if the weather cooperates. That's a bit better than last year because I'm not cutting back on fertilizer.
